comments.text:
Created attachment 3270
Suggested patch

Every now and then there is an R-help post with non-breakable spaces in their otherwise reproducible example ([e.g.](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2023-November/478518.html)). Currently, trying to parse R code containing NBSPs results in cryptic-looking errors:

```
parse(text = 'x <- \ua0 42')
# Error in parse(text = "x <-  42") : <text>:1:6: unexpected input
# 1: x <-  
#          ^
```

The parser tries to do the right thing by skipping anything that tests positive for `iswblank()`. Unfortunately, [NBSPs are `iswpunct()`, not `iswblank()`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/50955136), by design.

Since there is already a special case for skipping NBSPs on Windows when running with an 8-bit locale, let's implement a few more for when we know that `wchar_t` corresponds to Unicode code points.

I've tried to add a regression test, but there's no easy way to test for `defined(__STDC_ISO_10646__) || (defined(__APPLE__) || defined(__FreeBSD__) || defined(__sun)` from the R code. If `l10n_info()[['UTF-8']]` does not actually correlate to `wchar_t` being Unicode, it may be better to drop this test.

comments.creator: maechler
comments.text:
Thank you, Ivan.   Your patch works fine, I applied and tried it just for yet-another example I got in an e-mail.

You have well classified this as  `[Wishlist]` as indeed, I am not sure if we should do / provide this.

Often (also in the case mentioned above), the non-breakable space characters are the only non-ASCII characters  in R code, and we still *do* emphasize that for portability ASCII R code may be quite desirable.
For that reason, I think such NBSP character should be replaced by regular `' '` (space),  and at least for Emacs users as me that's easy and fast (*and* emacs shows the NBSP characters to me as kind of underscores, so I can easily notice).

An alternative solution to the problem maybe a small utils pkg function which replaces all NBSP by SP in a file / textConnection, so users can do this quickly, and R GUIs could do it semi-automatically for an R script or "pasted R code"
{user opt-in I'd prefer}.

Such a function maybe very short, basically calling  `chartr('\ua0', ' ', <line>)`
i.e., something like
```
fixNBSP <- function(con) writeLines(vapply(readLines(con), \(ln) chartr('\ua0', ' ', ln), ".."), con)
```

On second thought, I agree that the need for this is not dire enough to patch the parser. I had assumed that Unicode-native languages like Python3 and Perl5 skip NBSPs like other spaces, but that turns out to be not the case:

```
% printf '1  +\ua0 1' | lua5.3 # not Unicode-native
lua5.3: stdin:1: unexpected symbol near '1'
% printf '1  +\ua0 1' | perl -Mutf8
Unrecognized character \x{a0}; marked by <-- HERE after 1  +<-- HERE near column 5 at - line 1.
% printf '1  +\ua0 1' | python3
  File "<stdin>", line 1
    1  +  1
        ^
SyntaxError: invalid character in identifier
```

So the only positive precedent we have is skipping NBSPs on Windows with 8-bit encodings, and that's becoming increasingly obscure.

I'll see if there is a way to make the R error message less cryptic, closer to what Perl5 says, without breaking other cases.
